newsitem.title: NORWAY: Divers probe oil risk by grounded cruise liner. [CORRECTED 12:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Divers probe oil risk by grounded cruise liner. [CORRECTED 12:20 GMT]

text.p: Divers looked for signs of an oil spill on Monday near a Bahamian-registered Hanseatic cruise liner that ran aground off the Arctic island of Spitzbergen, Norwegian rescue officials said.

The Norwegian Pollution Directorate and the coast guard (deleting reference to centre in Bodoe) planned to decide later if it was necessary to unload the ship's fuel before trying to pull the vessel free.

The Hanseatic, carrying 145 mainly German tourists, ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off the north coast of Spitzbergen. No one was hurt and there was only slight damage to the hull at midships, rescue officials said.
But the ship was carrying 480 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, 35 tonnes of diesel and 10 tonnes of gasoline.
"The authorities are considering whether the fuel should be discharged before they try to tow her free tomorrow," Steinar Breivik, duty officer at the rescue centre, told Reuters.
"There has not been any leakage so far but they must investigate because most of the area around Spitzbergen is a conservation area."
All passengers and crew were still aboard the liner, which had been on its way from Norway to Iceland.
The 9,000-deadweight-tonne vessel is owned by Hanseatic Tours, a subsidiary of Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd Cruiseship Management GmbH.
A Swedish passenger ship, Origo, unsuccessfully tried to pull the Hanseatic free and was waiting alongside. Two coastguard vessels were due to arrive later on Monday.
Norway's NTB news agency said the Finnish-built Hanseatic had previously run aground last August off the Canadian coast in the Arctic with 268 people on board.
